text: Why are three separate network diagrams standard practice rather than one?
choices: Each answers a different question — what is plugged into what, what talks to what in which segment, and how traffic gets between segments — and separating them is what makes each maintainable
explanation: One diagram containing everything becomes unreadable, impossible to keep current, and answers no question well. The physical diagram is the one you want at 03:14 and carries no IP addresses at all.
